column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/cargo-publish-each-member-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS. The workflow has TWO jobs — `release` (bump + publish + tag,
# all three inside one composite action) and `publish-withheld` (the notice
# that makes the privacy guard's skip audible). They partition the human-actor
# case: exactly one of them runs, never both, never neither. Two axes move the
# selection — actor (bot vs human) and the privacy pair
# (github.event.repository.private × inputs.publish-from-private) — and
# everything else this table declares is pinned deliberately as a NEGATIVE: to
# record which inputs do NOT move the selection, so a future edit that makes one
# of them matter shows up as a diff here instead of as a silent behaviour
# change.
# WHY IT EXISTS — and the finding it records. This file is part of the sweep
# opened by graphql-synthesizer on 2026-08-08: a release workflow reported
# SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, published nothing, and nothing said so,
# because its ship job carried `&& !github.event.repository.private`. Every
# `*-auto-release*.yml` in substrate carries a `repository.private` guard, so
# each was swept for that silent-no-publish shape.
# THE PREVIOUS VERSION OF THIS FILE RECORDED THE INVERSE, AND THE FLIP IS THE
# WHOLE REVIEW SIGNAL. Until 2026-08-17 this workflow had NO privacy guard at
# all: its single `github.event.repository.private` occurrence was in `runs-on`,
#   runs-on: ${{ github.event.repository.private && (vars.PRIVATE_BUILDER_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest') || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
# which selects a RUNNER LABEL (a reusable workflow's runs-on bills the CALLER,
# so a metered label here charges every private consumer) and gates nothing. A
# private caller therefore DID publish to crates.io, and the row asserting that
# was named `private-human-push-STILL-PUBLISHES`. The old header said: "If a
# privacy guard is ever added to this workflow, the private row must flip to
# expect-skip in the SAME commit — that flip is the whole review signal." That
# is this commit; `private-human-push-WITHHELD` below is that row, flipped.
# WHAT THE GUARD COSTS HERE, stated because it is NOT the same as in the
# sibling workflows. cargo-auto-release and npm-auto-release split bump from
# ship, so their guard withholds only the publish and their withheld-notice
# truthfully says "the version was bumped and tagged". This workflow does all
# three inside ONE composite action — pleme-io/actions/cargo-publish-each-member
# runs bump -> publish -> commit-tag, and commit-tag fires only AFTER a
# successful publish, deliberately, so git can never tag a version absent from
# the registry. Withholding the publish therefore withholds the bump and the tag
# with it. The `release` row flipping to expect-skip is asserting all three
# withheld, not just the upload, and the notice's wording says so.
# THE BOT ROWS SELECT NEITHER JOB, ON PURPOSE. `publish-withheld` carries the
# same `github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'` clause `release` does, so the
# loop guard produces no notice. A loop-guard skip is not a withholding, and
# announcing it as one would train the operator to ignore the notice — which is
# the failure this whole layer exists to prevent, re-created one level up.
# NO no-bump ROW, deliberately. The bump/skip-when-no-source-changes decision
# lives inside the composite action's steps, per workspace member, and is
# invisible to job selection: no `needs.*.outputs.bumped` exists to model. A
# fabricated no-bump row would assert nothing and read as coverage. The
# `skip-when-no-source-changes` axis is unassertable at this layer — see the
# workflow's own inputs.
# always() is now READ, not merely supplied: publish-withheld's condition opens
# with it. It is not load-bearing here (that job has no `needs:` to be dragged
# down by), and the workflow comment says so rather than overclaiming — it is
# present so the day a `needs:` lands, the notice does not silently re-bury
# itself.
# Baseline: a human push on a PUBLIC repo. release runs and publishes; there is
# nothing to withhold, so the notice stands down.
public-human-push
# THE ROW WORTH READING, and the one that flipped. A private caller no longer
# publishes — and the run says so out loud instead of concluding green over an
# empty registry. Contrast the same row before 2026-08-17, which asserted
# `release` RAN here.
private-human-push-WITHHELD
# The escape hatch, asserted rather than documented. A private source that
# deliberately produces public crates opts in, and gets the pre-guard behaviour
# back exactly — release runs, no notice. Without this row the guard would be
# indistinguishable from an unconditional private ban.
private-human-push-opt-in
# The opt-in is INERT on a public repo: it can only ever widen the private arm,
# never narrow the public one. Pinned as a negative so an edit that made the
# input gate public publishing too would surface here.
public-human-push-opt-in-is-inert
# The loop guard: the action pushes per-member tags, a tag push re-triggers the
# caller, and the bot must not publish again. NEITHER job selects — see the
# header on why the notice deliberately stays quiet here.
bot-actor-no-publish-loop
# Same guard on a private repo — the actor check is visibility-independent, and
# it dominates the privacy guard rather than composing with it.
bot-actor-private-no-publish-loop
# The loop guard also dominates the OPT-IN: a repo that opted into publishing
# from private source still must not let the bot's own tag push re-publish.
bot-actor-private-opt-in-still-no-loop
# A non-push trigger (a caller wiring this to workflow_dispatch or schedule)
# changes nothing: event_name is pinned as a negative, per the header.
human-dispatch-still-runs
# ...and the guard is trigger-independent too: a dispatch on a private repo is
# withheld and announced exactly like a push.
private-dispatch-withheld
